text:
incident_bot: ALERT: spike in 502/504 errors from gateway cluster us-west-2 — 4xx->5xx ratio up 8x, triggered page to #incidents
kim: I'm on it. seeing a jump in 502s starting ~06:12 UTC. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/s/ingress/gateway-errors
alvaro: assigning pager to @sre-oncall — please post initial impact and ETA for mitigation.
sre-oncall: taking it. quick summary: 502 spike concentrated on /api/v1/generate proxies; p50 latency normal but p95 shoots to 8-12s, timeouts upstream. customer-facing errors (500/502) increasing.
maria: Support flagged a handful of customers seeing "gateway timeout" in logs, one enterprise customer reported failures in batch jobs. working on impact list.
kim: triage notes: ingress (nginx-ingress) returning 502s when upstream auth service times out. however we have poor trace coverage for these requests — Jaeger shows <0.5% sampling for gateway so we don't have spans for most failed flows.
nadeem: real-time plan: 1) increase trace sampling to 100% for gateway for 20m window 2) enable debug-level logging on gateway pods 3) temporarily bump proxy_read_timeout and upstream timeouts 4) if needed, route a small percentage of traffic around auth service for critical customers
jen: +1. anything we toggle must be timeboxed and reverted. also need a runbook step to add request_id header propagation — most traces missing traceparent since gateway strips it sometimes.
opsbot: ACTION: created incident INC-2026, severity P1, runbook link: https://wiki.redwood/internal/incidents/inc-2026
kim: executing steps now. patching deployment to set OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER=always_on and LOG_LEVEL=debug on nginx-ingress controller. running:
```bash
kubectl -n ingress patch deploy nginx-ingress -p '{"spec":{"template":{"spec":{"containers":[{"name":"nginx","env":[{"name":"OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER","value":"always_on"},{"name":"LOG_LEVEL","value":"debug"}]}]}}}}'
```
kim: also applying a short-lived ConfigMap change to nginx to bump proxy_read_timeout to 30s (was 10s) and proxy_connect_timeout to 15s. reload triggered.
alvaro: tagging support-esc with ETA messaging. support-esc, prepare a short customer note: we're experiencing intermittent gateway errors impacting text generation endpoints; engineers are actively mitigating, next update in 20m.
support-esc: drafting now. will send to impacted list once we have confirmation window.
maria: checking traces after patch — seeing new spans but many requests still show no traceparent. investigating whether the auth proxy is dropping the header.
kim: running tcpdump on auth-proxy to confirm header propagation surface: `kubectl exec -n auth-proxy pod/auth-proxy-7f9 -- tcpdump -A -s 0 'tcp port 443 and host auth-upstream'`
nadeem: quick check: gateway error logs show "upstream prematurely closed connection" and backend returning 502 body from envoy. Could be request size + header bloat + auth latency.
jen: useful stopgap: add a temporary header whitelist to strip non-essential headers to reduce header size. also increase max header size on nginx.
kim: applied header whitelist (X-Forwarded-For, Authorization, traceparent, x-rw-customer). also bumped large_client_header_buffers size.
opsbot: NOTE: debug logging will increase log volume significantly; forwarding retention will be reduced for the next hour to avoid S3 storm.
alvaro: update: after sampling and header whitelist, error rate dropped ~60% in 8 minutes. p95 latency back down to ~3s.
maria: support-esc: you can now send update: "We implemented temporary mitigations; rate of failures reduced but some customers may still see intermittent errors. Engineers will continue monitoring and follow up."
support-esc: sent. copied legal and account teams for enterprise customers.
kim: root cause hypothesis: auth service experiencing slowdowns under spiky metadata header sizes; combined with low proxy timeouts -> nginx returns 502. Observability gap: trace sampling was too low and gateway sometimes stripped traceparent, so we couldn't correlate spans.
nadeem: permanent actions (short list): 1) ensure traceparent propagation end-to-end and set sampling to a sensible default (1-2%) with 100% on errors 2) add an ingress dashboard for header size and auth latency 3) alert on sudden drop in sampling coverage 4) bake a runbook step to toggle timeouts safely
jen: opened follow-up ticket INFRA-4123 to add trace-id propagation tests to CI and add integration test with auth-proxy.
kim: created a small PR to add a temporary stopgap logging line in the gateway that logs upstream response body on 5xx for 10 minutes; PR link: https://git.redwood/internal/nginx/merge/1234
maria: request from legal: list of impacted customers and timestamps. sharing CSV shortly.
alvaro: handoff: @sre-oncall will monitor for 1 hour, revert debug env and reduced retention in 40m if stable. @kim will stay for rollback after window.
sre-oncall: acknowledged. monitoring dashboard pinned. will update every 10m or on change.
opsbot: RESOLUTION: error rate back to baseline after mitigations; monitoring in watch window.
kim: postmortem notes to add: - Why trace sampling default was too low - Why gateway stripped traceparent in some requests - Add header-size metrics and alerting - Consider graceful auth bypass for critical customers during auth infra incidents - Add playbook for temporary sampling/logging toggles
jen: one last action: schedule follow-up meeting with auth, gateway, infra, and support to verify permanent fixes. tentative: tomorrow 15:00 UTC.
maria: I will compile the incident timeline and impact email draft for CS.
alvaro: thanks team — great fast coordination. please move items to INC-2026 and close this thread once postmortem PR is ready. :thumbsup:
